`tests/test_cbsp.py` now has a real-fixture parity test that skips when the generated/licensed build artifact is absent. With the local artifact present, it checks each typed name target is within CTAG and NUL-terminated within 256 bytes, computes Python’s materialized expected bytes, then runs the PS2 C decoder/materializer on the same packaged CBSP and CTAG image. The C output matches byte-for-byte. The existing synthetic C fixture remains in place.

The PS2 `ps2_cbsp_materialize` interface now receives the CTAG image bytes as well as its target base and extent. Before writing the output image, it checks every domain-1 target for a bounded NUL terminator; `ps2_cache.c` supplies the already materialized tag-cache base. Python `CbspImage.materialize` applies the same name rule, rejects virtual BSP/CTAG overlap, and Python CBSP encoding rejects unaligned relocation slots to match the C parser. Regression coverage includes overlap, unterminated names, unaligned fields, and an unchanged destination on C rejection. The relevant implementation is in `tools/cbsp.py`, `submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/include/ps2_cbsp.h`, `submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/src/ps2_cbsp.c`, and its production caller `submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/src/ps2_cache.c`.

`python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_cbsp.py tests/test_ctag_schema_walk.py` passed (26 tests). This included the actual Blood Gulch HP2 artifact and host-compiled `ps2_cbsp.c`. The result compares all 1,296,384 materialized bytes; the unchanged bytes remain unchanged and each recorded pointer is rebased by its declared domain. `python3 tools/hcu_ps2_closure.py --layer all --no-bootstrap-memory` also passed target compilation: `compiled_count=369`, `failed_count=0`, R5900 GCC `15.2.0`, manifest SHA-256 `8fa834f2185dd9dae225c51ef236d6491e2ab9449c3e6f7cc9eb2eb7c407485a`. Added a package-backed fixture that compares CE's sound-scenery scenario-object path against the raw sound-scenery placement and palette blocks in all 13 pinned stock Halo CE multiplayer maps. The fixture calls the actual CE `object_new_from_scenario` implementation and actual `sound_scenery_new` / `sound_scenery_delete` callbacks. Its narrow test seams replace the live object-pool allocation and type-placement boundary; it is not a full simulation, audio, or PS2-target test.

Map census: 13 placements total—Blood Gulch 2, Beaver Creek 8, Damnation 3; the other ten maps have zero. There are three nonempty sound-scenery palettes, one per map with placements. Every source placement has an unnamed entry (`name_index == NONE`) and an in-range palette index; the palette group is `ssce` and its reference resolves to a sound-scenery tag. Each map is tested across both scenario-load cycles in the inherited 13-map host lifecycle matrix. For every placement, the test independently checks all ten raw 32-bit words, selected palette reference, CE-generated position/orientation/variant, object placement callback, and the sound-scenery callback lifecycle.

The source explains the scope of this result. `object_new_from_scenario` validates palette/name state, obtains the referenced definition, builds placement data from the scenario position/rotation/variant, creates the object, then places it (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c:4035`). The sound-scenery definition registers the `ssce` group, scenario block offsets and stride, and the new/delete callbacks (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/object_types.c:375`). CE's `sound_scenery_new` sets the object's shadowless flag; delete does nothing (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/sound/sound_scenery.c:30`). Thus this fixture validates object placement/lifecycle setup, not an emitted sound. No SPU2 request, sound playback, runtime audio asset, real object pool admission, in-game rendering, or EE/PCSX2 result is claimed.

Result: `1 passed in 85.89s`. The test compiles an ILP32 host harness and runs the inherited package-backed CE scenario/BSP matrix for all 13 stock maps and two cycles. verbatim_lines.raw: Added and ran a separate host diagnostic over all 13 pinned stock multiplayer maps. It combines two previously separate proofs:

2. The actual render/texcache.c implementation allocates the resources in BSP-texture, lightmap-slot, then object-texture key order. The fixture feeds the same top-level mip data and CLUT sizes as the production callbacks, the renderer's 270-page NTSC cache capacity, 127 CLUT slots, and the 1.5 MiB per-frame upload budget. It scans all resources for two consecutive frame numbers and records uploads, hits, deferrals, and occupied-page high-water.

All maps completed both scans with zero TC_FULL failures, owner and scratch bounds intact, outer canaries intact, and cache flush/owner rewind verified. Blood Gulch is the closest RAM owner at 3,954,720 / 4,014,928 bytes (60,208 bytes free). Sidewinder is 3,697,632 bytes. Blood Gulch's conservative all-resource pass deferred two uploads in frame 0; frame 1 accepted those two, with the other 76 resources as cache hits. Thus the candidate is tight but this resource set did not reveal an intrinsically uncacheable texture or permanent upload-budget starvation.

owner is the high-water of co-resident converted section data in the candidate render owner. cache high-water is occupied texture pages under the actual renderer cache API; the 270-page limit reflects the current 512x448 NTSC mode and renderer's reserved pages, as derived below. uploads / hits / deferred list frame 0 then frame 1.

The runtime emits one row per map with scratch high-water 98,304 / 524,288 bytes. Selected MODL coverage ranged from 4 models / 23 parts on Putput to 25 models / 163 parts on Blood Gulch; these are converter model-section counts, not spawned-object counts.

- The production world.c:21-37 callback supplies mip 0, its pixel bytes, and the CLUT; world.c:43-57 supplies lightmap page pixels and the shared 1,024-byte CLUT. This fixture uses those same parser views.

- submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/render/bsp_render.c:29-33 reserves 16 texture-window pages for CLUTs and one for the font. Its pages_for and resident_tex0 at :344-382 compute page occupancy, charge pixel-plus-CLUT upload bytes, request a cache entry, and enqueue the real GS upload pair. :800-802 and :832-840 establish texture/lightmap/object key ordering and the 1.5 MiB budget.

- The page count used by the diagnostic follows platform/video.h (512x448, 4 MiB GS VRAM) and platform/video.c:14-29: the two CT16 framebuffers and Z24 buffer consume 1,835,008 bytes (224 GS pages), and bsp_render.c:164 starts the texture window after the extra allocated page. 512 total GS pages - 224 framebuffer/Z pages - 1 window-base page - 17 CLUT/font pages = 270 cache pages.

- Halo-64's `submodules/halo-64/port/n64/NOTES.md:115-155` is a useful comparison for why its texture policy cannot be copied: its first-person atlas had to be split into windows and represented as small CI4 textures, while it also describes tradeoffs around its level texture path. This measurement instead uses this repository's halo-ps2 GS/VRAM/cache implementation and its 270-page renderer window; no N64 texture or pool limit is imported.

verbatim_lines.raw: The CE cluster lens-flare selector was compiled from the pinned source and exercised against the raw BSP images for all 13 stock Halo CE multiplayer maps. The independent host oracle agrees with CE's emitted marker-index sequence for every cluster. Only Boarding Action, Damnation, and Putput contain a non-empty lens-flare marker palette in these BSP images; they account for 1,121 valid marker submissions (207 + 22 + 892). The other ten maps have empty marker arrays and correctly submit none.

This closes a source-backed selector/data-range subcheck for the lens-flare marker consumer. It does not establish that flares are visibly rendered, that definitions resolve to the intended bitmap/effect, that occlusion queries work, or that the production PS2 renderer submits the data. It is not Step 7 or Step 8 closure evidence by itself.

The exercised CE function is `rasterizer_lens_flare_submit_for_cluster()` in `submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/rasterizer/rasterizer_lights.c:771-840`. It obtains the selected cluster, bounds its marker scan to the BSP marker count and the signed-short index capacity (`:779-798`), validates each marker's lens-flare palette index (`:799-806`), decodes the marker direction into the submit parameters, and forwards the selected record (`:808-835`). The record layout is defined in the same file: a 12-byte position, three signed direction bytes, and one palette-index byte (`:288-295`); compile-time assertions in that source pin the cluster and marker ABI sizes.

`tests/test_hcu_mp_lens_flare_all_maps.py` reuses the existing source extractor, raw BSP decoder, and ABI shim in `tests/test_hcu_mp_lens_flare_consumer.py`, while supplying the full 13-map source-digest allowlist. The test extracts the function body from the current HCU source, substitutes only the debug-option global with a host stub, then compiles it with the retail BSP blocks and CE-sized structure shims. A recording submit function captures the indices CE forwards. The Python oracle independently reads each cluster's first-marker/count words at `0x40/0x42`, walks the decoded marker block, and filters marker palette references against the BSP lens-flare palette count. It compares the full ordered index sequence, not only totals.
All files are decompressed retail `.map` artifacts at `build/retail-maps/decompressed/<name>.map`. Their SHA-256 digests are checked before parsing and are embedded in the test.
| Map | BSP clusters | Lens-flare palette entries | Marker records | Valid CE marker submissions | Raw map SHA-256 |
Result: **3 passed in 1.97s**. `git diff --check -- tests/test_hcu_mp_lens_flare_all_maps.py` passed. The all-map test alone had also passed before the synthetic subcase was added.
- No PCSX2 or hardware screenshot, GS/VU packet, sprite texture residency, occlusion-query result, or frame-time measurement was captured.

The CE structure-BSP detail-object path has now been exercised in a bounded source-derived host fixture. The 13 stock multiplayer BSPs all contain one `structure_detail_object_data` root record, but each root has `valid == 0` and all four child blocks (`cells`, `detail_objects`, `counts`, `z_reference_vectors`) are empty. The actual CE consumer therefore issues no detail-object rasterizer calls for any stock MP map. This identifies the currently shipped MP behavior precisely; it is not a finding that these BSP fields are disposable.

The same fixture injects the verbatim HCU camera-cell selector and its binary-search/count helpers and reaches a synthetic valid-data case. That case checks the 3×3 horizontal neighborhood, ±1 vertical cell selection, per-layer count/object offsets, scenario palette truncation, same-cell selection caching, an empty-but-valid data block, and the `local_player_count() == 1` gate. The test covers CPU-side view selection only; it does not draw the detail sprites, implement the PS2 rasterizer path, or demonstrate target-sized/EE execution.

- HCU `structure_render_detail_objects` is called in the world render flow at [`render.c:410`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/render/render.c#L410). The consumer is restricted to one local player and derives the camera cell from camera position at [`structure_detail_objects.c:420-437`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L420). For valid data it rebuilds when the camera cell changes or the dirty bit is set; the queried x/y coordinates cover a 3×3 neighborhood and z is limited to ±1 at [`structure_detail_objects.c:441-499`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L441). It caps cells per layer, validates count/object extents, uses the default z-reference when needed, and omits layers absent from the scenario palette at [`structure_detail_objects.c:501-543`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L501) and [`structure_detail_objects.c:556-587`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L556).

- Halo-64's comparison implementation follows the same one-player camera-cell and layer-selection shape at [`structure_detail_objects.c:376-399`](../../submodules/halo-64/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L376), then searches and builds cells at [`structure_detail_objects.c:410-479`](../../submodules/halo-64/source/structures/structure_detail_objects.c#L410). Its shown implementation directly dereferences the detail root, uses `cells.count - 1`, trusts count indices and counts, and increments layer cell arrays without the HCU guards. This is a useful comparison, not a reason to remove HCU bounds checks.

`tests/test_hcu_mp_detail_object_consumer.py` extracts the HCU comparator, lower/upper-bound, player-data, count-safety, and `structure_render_detail_objects` function bodies directly from the pinned source, compiles them into `tests/hcu_mp_detail_object_consumer_main.c`, then runs the CPU-only checks. For the retail inventory it decodes original decompressed Xbox map bytes using the Halo PS2 map/tag index tools, follows the retail structure-BSP pointer at the source-defined `detail_object_data` field, validates the root/child extents, and supplies the observed validity state to the verbatim CE consumer. Each map source SHA-256 is pinned in the test.

Result on 2026-10-22: `1 passed, 13 subtests passed`. The synthetic fixture reported successful camera-cell selection, layer/palette filtering, cache reuse, and the split-screen gate. Each of the 13 retail map subtests reported `detail_valid=0`, zero child blocks, and `draw_calls=0`.

The retail-map results mean detail-object camera-cell selection has no populated stock MP input to exercise: it is dormant for these 13 retail BSPs, not proven unnecessary for arbitrary/custom maps. Keep the BSP root and child blocks through conversion unless a separate compatibility decision covers modded content. The synthetic fixture is a controlled branch test, not a retail oracle. It does not qualify Xbox detail-object sprite/bitmap/material behavior, the HCU platform rasterizer implementation, GS memory or DMA, 2–4-player rendering beyond confirming CE's early return, target RAM high-water, frame cost, or PCSX2/EE behavior. Accordingly this closes only the source inventory and bounded CPU selection subcheck; it does not close Step 7's broader BSP-consumer or Step 8 target acceptance gates.

Added a package-backed fixture that compares CE's sound-scenery scenario-object path against the raw sound-scenery placement and palette blocks in all 13 pinned stock Halo CE multiplayer maps. The fixture calls the actual CE `object_new_from_scenario` implementation and actual `sound_scenery_new` / `sound_scenery_delete` callbacks. Its narrow test seams replace the live object-pool allocation and type-placement boundary; it is not a full simulation, audio, or PS2-target test.

Map census: 13 placements total—Blood Gulch 2, Beaver Creek 8, Damnation 3; the other ten maps have zero. There are three nonempty sound-scenery palettes, one per map with placements. Every source placement has an unnamed entry (`name_index == NONE`) and an in-range palette index; the palette group is `ssce` and its reference resolves to a sound-scenery tag. Each map is tested across both scenario-load cycles in the inherited 13-map host lifecycle matrix. For every placement, the test independently checks all ten raw 32-bit words, selected palette reference, CE-generated position/orientation/variant, object placement callback, and the sound-scenery callback lifecycle.

The source explains the scope of this result. `object_new_from_scenario` validates palette/name state, obtains the referenced definition, builds placement data from the scenario position/rotation/variant, creates the object, then places it (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c:4035`). The sound-scenery definition registers the `ssce` group, scenario block offsets and stride, and the new/delete callbacks (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/object_types.c:375`). CE's `sound_scenery_new` sets the object's shadowless flag; delete does nothing (`submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/sound/sound_scenery.c:30`). Thus this fixture validates object placement/lifecycle setup, not an emitted sound. No SPU2 request, sound playback, runtime audio asset, real object pool admission, in-game rendering, or EE/PCSX2 result is claimed.

Result: `1 passed in 85.89s`. The test compiles an ILP32 host harness and runs the inherited package-backed CE scenario/BSP matrix for all 13 stock maps and two cycles. The relevant persistent run output is `build/m2-mp-sound-scenery-runtime-final/run.log`; it contains 26 per-map-cycle success rows. This binary is a host test artifact, not the PS2 game ELF.

- This result covers only the sound-scenery placement consumer. It does not complete the BSP field/consumer inventory, collision topology coverage, relocation failure atomicity, or Step 8 capacity gates.

It scans all resources for two consecutive frame numbers and records uploads, hits, deferrals, and occupied-page high-water.

All maps completed both scans with zero TC_FULL failures, owner and scratch bounds intact, outer canaries intact, and cache flush/owner rewind verified. Blood Gulch is the closest RAM owner at 3,954,720 / 4,014,928 bytes (60,208 bytes free). Sidewinder is 3,697,632 bytes. Blood Gulch's conservative all-resource pass deferred two uploads in frame 0; frame 1 accepted those two, with the other 76 resources as cache hits. Thus the candidate is tight but this resource set did not reveal an intrinsically uncacheable texture or permanent upload-budget starvation.

owner is the high-water of co-resident converted section data in the candidate render owner. cache high-water is occupied texture pages under the actual renderer cache API; the 270-page limit reflects the current 512x448 NTSC mode and renderer's reserved pages, as derived below. uploads / hits / deferred list frame 0 then frame 1.

verbatim_lines.raw: Decision: the existing map-capacity diagnostic cannot yet be promoted into a multiplayer workload/high-water fixture by adding counters alone. Its current control flow deliberately stops before CE map-game initialization and simulation. The real CE entry points are known, but the diagnostic profile lacks a test-only bridge to them and no explicit bot-spawn workload is wired in. Keep Step 8 open; do not change any pool size or production owner budget from this inspection.

The target diagnostic runs after global `game_initialize()` and connection setup ([`main.c:3461-3477`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L3461)). That global initializer does create the fixed CE owners once—objects, players, particles/effects, and AI among them ([`game.c:281-325`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L281)). The opt-in hook then calls the lifecycle test, and the UI diagnostic profile intentionally enters an infinite loop rather than the ordinary main/game frame loop.

Inside that hook, the current 13-map test preflights and calls `scenario_load()` directly, reads PVS/collision, then calls `scenario_unload()` ([`ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:52-63`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L52), [`:76-141`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L76)). It does **not** call `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, create local player datums, call `objects_place()`/`ai_place()`, or run a game tick. Its completion marker is explicitly `query_only=1`. Therefore it measures map/tag/BSP owners and selected query state, not live object, player, weapon, projectile, effect, or bot occupancy.

The normal path is concrete: `main_new_map()` in `main.c` calls `game_load()`, then `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, creates local players, starts game time, and issues an initial pulse ([`main.c:1478-1505`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1478)). It is `static`, so the separate test translation unit cannot call it today. During `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, CE initializes per-map subsystems, marks the game active, places scenario objects, and calls `ai_place()` ([`game.c:663-729`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L663)). `ai_place()` delegates to `encounters_create_for_new_map()`, which iterates scenario-authored encounters and creates those not marked “not initially created” ([`ai.c:548-553`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/ai.c#L548), [`encounters.c:1730-1753`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/encounters.c#L1730)). This can measure actual scenario placement/AI work; it does not by itself create an arbitrary configured MP bot population.

The test-only path should therefore be a separate `STEP8_MP_WORKLOAD` profile—not an extension of the query-only marker—with a small bridge in `main.c` to invoke the real `main_new_map()` path. It must explicitly set and verify the selected connection/player mode, populate local player records through CE's helper, run deterministic frame/tick inputs, snapshot the already opt-in game-state/object-pool counters plus the distinct compatibility-malloc counters, and use normal per-map teardown before checking current usage/guards. The player fixture must assert spawned player/unit counts rather than trusting `player_spawn_count` alone. Object/weapon/effect churn must exercise the real CE calls and source tags; constructing arbitrary pool records by hand would not establish gameplay ownership.

- The all-13 content closure inventories tag references and offline converted sections; its own interpretation limits say bot count, effect peak, DMA staging and simultaneous runtime residency are not measured ([content closure](m2-step8-mp-match-time-content-closure-2026-10-22.md#L1)).

Next implementation order: (1) add the isolated workload profile and a test-only bridge to CE `main_new_map()`; (2) first run one map/one local player and prove player/unit spawn, object placement, simulation ticks, per-owner snapshots, unload/reset and canaries; (3) extend to the actual supported local-player modes and 13 maps; (4) only then define and exercise a genuine bot workload, including asset closure, and run both PCSX2 CPU modes plus retail R5900. Keep all HCU capacities, guards and the 5,767,168-byte reserve unchanged until measured evidence justifies a separately reviewed budget change. This memo establishes feasibility boundaries only; Step 8 remains open.

verbatim_lines.raw: Added opt-in allocator statistics behind `HALO_PS2_STEP8_MEMORY_DIAGNOSTIC`: capacity, current monotonic bytes used, high-water bytes, and failed arena allocations. In ordinary builds the diagnostic fields, API, and static counters are absent. The counters reset when a new physical-memory allocation interval begins and on teardown. The PS2 preboot SDK-heap path remains separate; overflow is rejected before it can reach that fallback.

`python3 tools/test_hcu_ps2_malloc_diagnostic.py` passed. The host fixture verifies preboot allocations remain untracked, 16-byte alignment, 48-byte high-water after requests of 17 and 1 bytes, monotonic behavior after free, arena-exhaustion and overflow failures, and reset after free/rebind. `git diff --check` passed. An R5900 compile check was unavailable because neither `mips64r5900el-ps2-elf-gcc` nor `ee-gcc` is installed in this environment.

The telemetry measures only the CE compatibility malloc arena mapped to `dynamic_simulation`. It does not include CE `game_state` allocations, the object memory pool, actor/prop/swarm arrays, graphics allocations, or GS/IOP stores. Thus it is instrumentation for a later live-match fixture, not evidence that the 2,621,440-byte pool fits bots, co-op, weapons, effects, or all 13 multiplayer maps.
- The diagnostic-only API and result fields: [`physical_memory_map.h:48-64`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/cache/physical_memory_map.h#L48)

The added compatibility-alignment and overflow-order guard preserves prior behavior and is test-covered. This subcheck does not close Step 8: target/runtime high-water, non-malloc owner peaks, maximum supported players/bots/co-op, rendering/DMA overlap, and target performance remain outstanding.

The HCU PS2 CE sources now expose separate diagnostic snapshots for the fixed CPU game-state arena and the CE fixed object-memory pool under `HALO_PS2_STEP8_MEMORY_DIAGNOSTIC` ([game-state counters/getter](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L181), [object-pool counters/getter](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L205), [diagnostic-only API](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/include/ps2_step8_memory_owners.h#L1)). Each snapshot has capacity, current used extent, high-water extent, and rejected-allocation count. The compatibility `malloc` arena remains a third, separate owner ([allocator telemetry](m2-step8-malloc-arena-telemetry-2026-10-22.md#L1)); this instrumentation does not charge or mutate it.

The game-state telemetry starts at `game_state_initialize()` and ends at `game_state_dispose()` ([lifecycle hooks](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L285), [initialization](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L1090)). Its monotonic cursor includes backing allocated to game-state data arrays and the CE object pool itself. The object-pool telemetry starts after `objects_initialize()` creates that pool and ends at `objects_dispose()` ([pool lifecycle](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1110), [pool reset](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1220)); its bytes are nested inside the game-state backing, so **do not add the two owners together**. Its `used_bytes` follows the memory pool's current cursor/highest-address extent (`memory_pool_get_used_size()`), including any holes below the last live block; it is a footprint/fragmentation measure, not a sum of live payload sizes. Map transitions keep the lifetime counters active and may lower current object-pool extent after frees; high-water remains for the subsystem lifetime.

The normal-profile objects contain no `ps2_step8_*` symbols or counter storage. The diagnostic profile's 24-byte `.bss` delta is the six 32-bit counters/active flags (three per owner); 620 bytes of additional `.text` are the guarded instrumentation and getters in these two objects. These are object-level deltas, not a linked-ELF or runtime memory report. The declarations/counters/instrumentation are all preprocessor-guarded; no structure layout or production ABI change was made. The whole PS2/gameplay ELF was not rebuilt with this new define, and no PCSX2 or retail EE workload was run.

- The next capacity evidence is a real supported multiplayer fixture that snapshots these owners and the compatibility arena through initialization, map transition, player/bot/co-op creation, representative weapon/effect churn, cleanup/reload, and failure handling on the 13-map set. Record current/high-water/failures per owner and keep game-state/object-pool nesting explicit. Do not claim 1–4 player or bot/co-op support from this primitive alone.

The focused host test and R5900 compile checks establish the diagnostic plumbing only. Step 8 remains open for runtime owner high-water, combined map/render/gameplay load, target placement/timing, and supported multiplayer workload evidence.

verbatim_lines.raw: Added and ran a separate host diagnostic over all 13 pinned stock multiplayer maps. It combines two previously separate proofs:

2. The actual render/texcache.c implementation allocates the resources in BSP-texture, lightmap-slot, then object-texture key order. The fixture feeds the same top-level mip data and CLUT sizes as the production callbacks, the renderer's 270-page NTSC cache capacity, 127 CLUT slots, and the 1.5 MiB per-frame upload budget. It scans all resources for two consecutive frame numbers and records uploads, hits, deferrals, and occupied-page high-water.

All maps completed both scans with zero TC_FULL failures, owner and scratch bounds intact, outer canaries intact, and cache flush/owner rewind verified. Blood Gulch is the closest RAM owner at 3,954,720 / 4,014,928 bytes (60,208 bytes free). Sidewinder is 3,697,632 bytes. Blood Gulch's conservative all-resource pass deferred two uploads in frame 0; frame 1 accepted those two, with the other 76 resources as cache hits. Thus the candidate is tight but this resource set did not reveal an intrinsically uncacheable texture or permanent upload-budget starvation.

owner is the high-water of co-resident converted section data in the candidate render owner. cache high-water is occupied texture pages under the actual renderer cache API; the 270-page limit reflects the current 512x448 NTSC mode and renderer's reserved pages, as derived below. uploads / hits / deferred list frame 0 then frame 1.

The runtime emits one row per map with scratch high-water 98,304 / 524,288 bytes. Selected MODL coverage ranged from 4 models / 23 parts on Putput to 25 models / 163 parts on Blood Gulch; these are converter model-section counts, not spawned-object counts.

- The production world.c:21-37 callback supplies mip 0, its pixel bytes, and the CLUT; world.c:43-57 supplies lightmap page pixels and the shared 1,024-byte CLUT. This fixture uses those same parser views.

- submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/render/bsp_render.c:29-33 reserves 16 texture-window pages for CLUTs and one for the font. Its pages_for and resident_tex0 at :344-382 compute page occupancy, charge pixel-plus-CLUT upload bytes, request a cache entry, and enqueue the real GS upload pair. :800-802 and :832-840 establish texture/lightmap/object key ordering and the 1.5 MiB budget.

- The page count used by the diagnostic follows platform/video.h (512x448, 4 MiB GS VRAM) and platform/video.c:14-29: the two CT16 framebuffers and Z24 buffer consume 1,835,008 bytes (224 GS pages), and bsp_render.c:164 starts the texture window after the extra allocated page. 512 total GS pages - 224 framebuffer/Z pages - 1 window-base page - 17 CLUT/font pages = 270 cache pages.

- Halo-64's `submodules/halo-64/port/n64/NOTES.md:115-155` is a useful comparison for why its texture policy cannot be copied: its first-person atlas had to be split into windows and represented as small CI4 textures, while it also describes tradeoffs around its level texture path. This measurement instead uses this repository's halo-ps2 GS/VRAM/cache implementation and its 270-page renderer window; no N64 texture or pool limit is imported.

verbatim_lines.raw: Decision: the existing map-capacity diagnostic cannot yet be promoted into a multiplayer workload/high-water fixture by adding counters alone. Its current control flow deliberately stops before CE map-game initialization and simulation. The real CE entry points are known, but the diagnostic profile lacks a test-only bridge to them and no explicit bot-spawn workload is wired in. Keep Step 8 open; do not change any pool size or production owner budget from this inspection.

The target diagnostic runs after global `game_initialize()` and connection setup ([`main.c:3461-3477`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L3461)). That global initializer does create the fixed CE owners once—objects, players, particles/effects, and AI among them ([`game.c:281-325`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L281)). The opt-in hook then calls the lifecycle test, and the UI diagnostic profile intentionally enters an infinite loop rather than the ordinary main/game frame loop.

Inside that hook, the current 13-map test preflights and calls `scenario_load()` directly, reads PVS/collision, then calls `scenario_unload()` ([`ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:52-63`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L52), [`:76-141`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L76)). It does **not** call `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, create local player datums, call `objects_place()`/`ai_place()`, or run a game tick. Its completion marker is explicitly `query_only=1`. Therefore it measures map/tag/BSP owners and selected query state, not live object, player, weapon, projectile, effect, or bot occupancy.

The normal path is concrete: `main_new_map()` in `main.c` calls `game_load()`, then `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, creates local players, starts game time, and issues an initial pulse ([`main.c:1478-1505`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1478)). It is `static`, so the separate test translation unit cannot call it today. During `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, CE initializes per-map subsystems, marks the game active, places scenario objects, and calls `ai_place()` ([`game.c:663-729`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L663)). `ai_place()` delegates to `encounters_create_for_new_map()`, which iterates scenario-authored encounters and creates those not marked “not initially created” ([`ai.c:548-553`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/ai.c#L548), [`encounters.c:1730-1753`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/encounters.c#L1730)). This can measure actual scenario placement/AI work; it does not by itself create an arbitrary configured MP bot population.

The test-only path should therefore be a separate `STEP8_MP_WORKLOAD` profile—not an extension of the query-only marker—with a small bridge in `main.c` to invoke the real `main_new_map()` path. It must explicitly set and verify the selected connection/player mode, populate local player records through CE's helper, run deterministic frame/tick inputs, snapshot the already opt-in game-state/object-pool counters plus the distinct compatibility-malloc counters, and use normal per-map teardown before checking current usage/guards. The player fixture must assert spawned player/unit counts rather than trusting `player_spawn_count` alone. Object/weapon/effect churn must exercise the real CE calls and source tags; constructing arbitrary pool records by hand would not establish gameplay ownership.

- The all-13 content closure inventories tag references and offline converted sections; its own interpretation limits say bot count, effect peak, DMA staging and simultaneous runtime residency are not measured ([content closure](m2-step8-mp-match-time-content-closure-2026-10-22.md#L1)).

Next implementation order: (1) add the isolated workload profile and a test-only bridge to CE `main_new_map()`; (2) first run one map/one local player and prove player/unit spawn, object placement, simulation ticks, per-owner snapshots, unload/reset and canaries; (3) extend to the actual supported local-player modes and 13 maps; (4) only then define and exercise a genuine bot workload, including asset closure, and run both PCSX2 CPU modes plus retail R5900. Keep all HCU capacities, guards and the 5,767,168-byte reserve unchanged until measured evidence justifies a separately reviewed budget change. This memo establishes feasibility boundaries only; Step 8 remains open.

The two surface collectors agree on every cluster. The all-cluster subcluster walk equals the union of the per-cluster sets. `structure_bsp_port_verify` accepts every relocated BSP. After the walks, the relocated image bytes match the post-fixup snapshot and the collision-user depth is 0.

Hangemhigh, longest, prisoner, and putput have zero cluster portals in the raw BSP (portal block count 0 and every cluster portal list empty). CE's portal loop and the direct `portal_hull_from_portal` sweep both observe that empty set. BSPS v2 portal count is 0.

Direct plane-index checks (`plane_ok`) equal the portal count on every map, including 0. Connectivity-walk plane checks (`traverse_plane_checks`), which run only when the neighbor is in range and in that cluster's PVS, are 130, 140, 276, 176, 28, 84, 0, 0, 0, 0, 60, 208, 80 in map order.

No HP2 under `build/` outside `build/emulator/runs/` contains a `BSP0` section; the capacity packages are CTAG/CBSP. The test generates a v2 `BSPS` section from each raw BSP with `submodules/halo-ps2/tools/halo2ps2/bspconv.py` (`convert_block` / `parse_section`). Per cluster, pack portal-list entries match the Xbox portal-index multiset, pack `cluster_a`/`cluster_b` match raw front/back (`0xFFFF` for -1), and pack triangle count matches the unique subcluster surface-set size. The section does not store CE surface ids, so the surface comparison is that cardinality.

verbatim_lines.raw: The bounded C candidate exactly replayed **226,395 operations from the real CE validator** during the a30/a50 package transaction fixture. Its peak was **4,820 merged intervals**, or 38,560 bytes of two-u32 interval payload. A fixed 8,192-record table (65,536 payload bytes) accommodated the complete captured trace without exhaustion. This supplies a concrete replacement candidate for the validation bitmap. The immediate integration target is multiplayer Longest/Blood Gulch and then the stock multiplayer corpus. This experiment does not establish production memory fit or target acceptance.

[`tools/hcu_claim_interval_experiment.py`](../../tools/hcu_claim_interval_experiment.py) implements exact half-open interval claims, byte membership/range intersection, BSP-domain clearing including interval splitting, adjacency merging, and checked 32-bit ranges. Capacity failure preserves the previous set. Ordinary overlap failure preserves CE's existing behavior, including its whole-word branch: a complete aligned 32-byte word is checked before any byte in that word is claimed. If byte 40 is already occupied, `claim(0,64)` claims only `[0,32)` before returning false. Tests explicitly cover conflicts at byte 1, 31 and 40, unaligned starts, and partial trailing words.

The Python and C tests include 12,000 and 40,000 deterministic operations against byte-bitmap models. A further test compiles the production `claim()` function verbatim with a bounded test-address provider and compares 30,000 operations with the candidate, checking every byte periodically. This direct source-function oracle guards against accidentally duplicating an incorrect interpretation of CE's whole-word branch.

Use a fresh trace name. The first sandbox run correctly failed after SIGSYS skips; the successful native experiment ran with approved execution outside that sandbox. Native test result: **1 unittest passed**, including both a30/a50 package subtests, **151.471 seconds**. This is the host ILP32 consumer/transaction fixture with deliberately oversized tag and BSP buffers.
| Single-point membership queries in retail trace | 0 |

All 226,395 operations replayed without a return-value mismatch. Single-byte membership is covered by the independent randomized fixture, rather than an actual retail call in this trace. The original bitmap's maximum configured capacity was 3,145,728 bytes (24 MiB address domain / 8); that value derives from the **host fixture**, and is not the PS2 production claims size. The candidate's measured peak pair payload is 38,560 bytes, while an 8,192-entry fixed-capacity implementation would reserve 65,536 bytes plus actual count/capacity/bookkeeping and any update workspace. Python's object allocations are not that C target store; no Python memory statistic is presented as an EE allocation.

The Python diagnostic uses sorted-vector copies. Its conservative comparison/copy work counter was **869,167,737**, and one complete host Python replay took **4.445 seconds**. The C backend instead performs **2,704,899 binary-search/clear comparisons** and moves **50,580,119 interval records / 404,640,952 bytes**, cumulatively over all five domain resets and repeated transaction cases. Host compile plus ctypes replay took **0.400 seconds** in one run. These figures are not EE cycles; load-time memory traffic requires target measurement. The captured trace proves the candidate's semantics and a30/a50 interval count.

The same backend compiles successfully for R5900 with `-O2 -std=gnu89 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`; the standalone object contains 1,936 text bytes, zero data and zero BSS. [`tests/hcu_claim_interval_layout.c`](../../tests/hcu_claim_interval_layout.c) also compiles with the target compiler, proving an eight-byte interval, 40-byte context and counter offset 24. Thus an 8,192-entry target table plus its context consumes **65,576 caller-owned bytes**, before any enclosing arena alignment/guard. The clear routine has two eight-byte local fragments; ordinary scalar/call stack remains a measured stack obligation. This proves object compilation and layout, not guest execution.

The wrappers for data arrays, object memory pools, and LRU caches all use that allocator ([game_state.c:860](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L860), [game_state.c:943](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L943)). The existing 1 MiB object pool is nested inside the 3,428,352-byte game-state binding ([objects.c:1050](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1050), [PS2 limits:18](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/include/halo_ps2_limits.h#L18)).

That contiguity is observable behavior: `game_state_image_contains()` rejects addresses outside the one game-state span; image pointers are calculated by subtracting the live base, and image acceptance copies the complete `GAME_STATE_SIZE` back over the live base ([game_state.c:650](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L650), [game_state.c:825](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L825)). A name-based arena branch would invalidate checkpoint validation and restoration unless those contracts change with it. Keeping the original complete allocation while routing another copy buys zero aggregate bytes.

The current parent binds the whole dynamic arena to the compatibility allocator, so it is not an unused secondary object pool ([hcu_memory_bind.c:60](../../src/stream/hcu_memory_bind.c#L60)). The allocator is a bounded bump store whose `free` does not reclaim individual allocations ([ps2_memory.c:300](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/src/ps2_memory.c#L300)). Carving a typed object store from it must reduce the compatibility span by precisely the same amount and prove all remaining compatibility allocations fit; the two cannot both own the same bytes.

The validator implements exact byte-set membership. `claim()` rejects any overlap and otherwise marks bytes, including a prefix before it detects a later overlap; its aligned-word branch checks all 32 bytes before claiming any byte in that word, which limits the failure prefix. `unclaim()` clears a range ([tag_validate.c:477](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/linux/game/tag_validate.c#L477)). `tag_validate_any_claimed()` is also used by the model-index validator ([tag_schema_models.c:443](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/linux/game/tag_schema_models.c#L443)). BSP activation clears only the BSP domain and deliberately preserves tag claims, including names ([tag_validate.c:1446](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/linux/game/tag_validate.c#L1446)). Therefore releasing all claims after CTAG validation breaks later BSP validation; a replacement must support the same union, overlap, range-clear, and membership behavior.

An exact sorted disjoint interval representation is a valid candidate: retain half-open byte ranges with adjacent ranges merged; query via binary search; split/remove intervals when clearing the BSP domain. Each interval needs at least two 32-bit offsets, eight bytes total, plus metadata and update workspace. A record-count bound and a checked capacity failure are mandatory. Arbitrary malformed input can alternate occupied/unoccupied bytes, so the worst-case interval representation can be larger than the bitmap. It must fail atomically and safely if its bounded table fills, and the required retail corpus must demonstrate a sufficient bound. Four-byte-granularity bitmaps are not equivalent because names and opaque data may occupy unaligned bytes.

Concrete next implementation: add a host diagnostic shadow interval set beside the existing bitmap. Replay every claim, clear and membership query from all 24 maps and 82 BSPs, compare every return and every range query, and record maximum live merged intervals, insertion shifts and scan cost. Preserve prefix mutation on failed claims if differential tests establish that callers observe it; otherwise explicitly prove failed validation resets all state before changing semantics. With a table of N intervals the exact replacement costs `8*N + metadata + workspace`; claiming any saving before measuring N is premature. Then implement the same bounded representation behind `HALO_PS2`, test overlap-at-first/middle/end, zero length, overflow, adjacent intervals, BSP clearing, stale-map rejection, exhaustion, and failure rollback. Target-cycle and physical-owner evidence remain separate gates.

The current full-image D20 lower bound is 30,087,556 bytes against 27,787,264 committed bytes, excluding texture, DMA, audio, streaming, scratch and other indispensable owners ([repartition review](m2-2026-10-21-budget-repartition-review.md)). Its claims are 2,320,580 bytes. Even the impossible ideal of **zero-byte claims** lowers that subtotal only to 27,766,976 bytes: 20,288 bytes remain for all omitted owners. An actual interval table reduces that margin further. Moving the object pool does not alter this arithmetic.

Its monotonic cursor includes backing allocated to game-state data arrays and the CE object pool itself. The object-pool telemetry starts after `objects_initialize()` creates that pool and ends at `objects_dispose()` ([pool lifecycle](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1110), [pool reset](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1220)); its bytes are nested inside the game-state backing, so **do not add the two owners together**. Its `used_bytes` follows the memory pool's current cursor/highest-address extent (`memory_pool_get_used_size()`), including any holes below the last live block; it is a footprint/fragmentation measure, not a sum of live payload sizes. Map transitions keep the lifetime counters active and may lower current object-pool extent after frees; high-water remains for the subsystem lifetime.

The normal-profile objects contain no `ps2_step8_*` symbols or counter storage. The diagnostic profile's 24-byte `.bss` delta is the six 32-bit counters/active flags (three per owner); 620 bytes of additional `.text` are the guarded instrumentation and getters in these two objects. These are object-level deltas, not a linked-ELF or runtime memory report. The declarations/counters/instrumentation are all preprocessor-guarded; no structure layout or production ABI change was made. The whole PS2/gameplay ELF was not rebuilt with this new define, and no PCSX2 or retail EE workload was run.

- The next capacity evidence is a real supported multiplayer fixture that snapshots these owners and the compatibility arena through initialization, map transition, player/bot/co-op creation, representative weapon/effect churn, cleanup/reload, and failure handling on the 13-map set. Record current/high-water/failures per owner and keep game-state/object-pool nesting explicit. Do not claim 1–4 player or bot/co-op support from this primitive alone.

The focused host test and R5900 compile checks establish the diagnostic plumbing only. Step 8 remains open for runtime owner high-water, combined map/render/gameplay load, target placement/timing, and supported multiplayer workload evidence.

verbatim_lines.raw: Decision: the existing map-capacity diagnostic cannot yet be promoted into a multiplayer workload/high-water fixture by adding counters alone. Its current control flow deliberately stops before CE map-game initialization and simulation. The real CE entry points are known, but the diagnostic profile lacks a test-only bridge to them and no explicit bot-spawn workload is wired in. Keep Step 8 open; do not change any pool size or production owner budget from this inspection.

The target diagnostic runs after global `game_initialize()` and connection setup ([`main.c:3461-3477`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L3461)). That global initializer does create the fixed CE owners once—objects, players, particles/effects, and AI among them ([`game.c:281-325`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L281)). The opt-in hook then calls the lifecycle test, and the UI diagnostic profile intentionally enters an infinite loop rather than the ordinary main/game frame loop.

Inside that hook, the current 13-map test preflights and calls `scenario_load()` directly, reads PVS/collision, then calls `scenario_unload()` ([`ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:52-63`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L52), [`:76-141`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c#L76)). It does **not** call `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, create local player datums, call `objects_place()`/`ai_place()`, or run a game tick. Its completion marker is explicitly `query_only=1`. Therefore it measures map/tag/BSP owners and selected query state, not live object, player, weapon, projectile, effect, or bot occupancy.

The normal path is concrete: `main_new_map()` in `main.c` calls `game_load()`, then `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, creates local players, starts game time, and issues an initial pulse ([`main.c:1478-1505`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1478)). It is `static`, so the separate test translation unit cannot call it today. During `game_initialize_for_new_map()`, CE initializes per-map subsystems, marks the game active, places scenario objects, and calls `ai_place()` ([`game.c:663-729`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L663)). `ai_place()` delegates to `encounters_create_for_new_map()`, which iterates scenario-authored encounters and creates those not marked “not initially created” ([`ai.c:548-553`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/ai.c#L548), [`encounters.c:1730-1753`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/encounters.c#L1730)). This can measure actual scenario placement/AI work; it does not by itself create an arbitrary configured MP bot population.

The test-only path should therefore be a separate `STEP8_MP_WORKLOAD` profile—not an extension of the query-only marker—with a small bridge in `main.c` to invoke the real `main_new_map()` path. It must explicitly set and verify the selected connection/player mode, populate local player records through CE's helper, run deterministic frame/tick inputs, snapshot the already opt-in game-state/object-pool counters plus the distinct compatibility-malloc counters, and use normal per-map teardown before checking current usage/guards. The player fixture must assert spawned player/unit counts rather than trusting `player_spawn_count` alone. Object/weapon/effect churn must exercise the real CE calls and source tags; constructing arbitrary pool records by hand would not establish gameplay ownership.

- The all-13 content closure inventories tag references and offline converted sections; its own interpretation limits say bot count, effect peak, DMA staging and simultaneous runtime residency are not measured ([content closure](m2-step8-mp-match-time-content-closure-2026-10-22.md#L1)).

Next implementation order: (1) add the isolated workload profile and a test-only bridge to CE `main_new_map()`; (2) first run one map/one local player and prove player/unit spawn, object placement, simulation ticks, per-owner snapshots, unload/reset and canaries; (3) extend to the actual supported local-player modes and 13 maps; (4) only then define and exercise a genuine bot workload, including asset closure, and run both PCSX2 CPU modes plus retail R5900. Keep all HCU capacities, guards and the 5,767,168-byte reserve unchanged until measured evidence justifies a separately reviewed budget change. This memo establishes feasibility boundaries only; Step 8 remains open.

verbatim_lines.raw: The PS2 production transition order is unsafe for a singleton CTAG-backed map owner. **CE `game_dispose_from_old_map()` must run before `game_unload()` when an old scenario is loaded.** On this port, `game_unload()` calls `scenario_unload()`, and the PS2 `scenario_unload()` path first clears the CE scenario/BSP globals and then calls `ps2_cache_release_map_owner()`. The parent callback unloads the CTAG mount/source and makes the old tag/BSP storage available for reuse. Calling CE disposal only afterward reverses the lifetime contract: old-map callbacks execute after the storage and global pointers they are meant to retire have been unpublished/released.
1. CE’s `game_unload()` only calls `scenario_unload()` when `game_globals->map_loaded` is true ([`game.c:754-785`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L754)).

2. CE’s `game_dispose_from_old_map()` performs map-derived cleanup—including structures, render objects, objects, players, effects, sound, and scenario cleanup—and calls `scenario_dispose_from_old_map()` near the end ([`game.c:946-984`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L946)).

3. `scenario_unload()` calls `scenario_tags_unload()`, clears `global_scenario`, `global_structure_bsp`, `global_collision_bsp`, `global_bsp3d`, and `global_game_globals`, then releases the PS2 parent map owner ([`scenario.c:387-425`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/scenario/scenario.c#L387)). `scenario_tags_unload()` closes tag consumers and clears the cache header/tag table publication before returning ([`cache_files.c:617-658`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/cache/cache_files.c#L617)).

6. Retail CE control flow independently corroborates disposal-before-unload: non-PS2 map transition code calls `game_dispose_from_old_map()` before `game_unload()` ([`main.c:1612-1621`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1612), [`main.c:1984-1988`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1984), and [`network_game_manager.c:801-805`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/networking/network_game_manager.c#L801)). The PS2-specific early-unload branches are the divergence.

The strongest concrete consequence is a dangling/invalid old-map lifetime at subsequent disposers. For example, `game_dispose_from_old_map()` calls `objects_dispose_from_old_map()` before `scenario_dispose_from_old_map()` ([`game.c:965-980`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L965)); object teardown walks and frees map-era object datums and invalidates cluster partitions ([`objects.c:1172-1205`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1172)). The sequence is designed as an ordered CE teardown, not as a harmless second idempotent clear after scenario unload. Not every individual callback has been proven to dereference a tag byte on every map, so the exact failure mechanism for a particular run is an inference; the ownership/lifetime violation itself is directly proven.
| Site | Classification | Present PS2 sequence | Audit disposition |

| `source/main/main.c:1612-1622`, `main_change_map_name()` | Production local map replacement | preflight → `game_unload()` → `game_dispose_from_old_map()` → precache successor → new map | **Fix required.** Keep preflight before mutation; reverse only the teardown pair to dispose old state while its tag owner is live, then unload/release it before successor materialization. Add a `port:` comment that states this ownership ordering. |

| `source/main/main.c:1974-1978`, `main_load_ui_scenario()` PS2 block | Production return-to-menu/UI map replacement | preflight UI → unload old map → dispose old state → precache UI | **Fix required.** Preserve preflight-before-teardown, then dispose-before-unload. This covers return from gameplay/co-op to UI. |

| `source/main/main.c:2912-2926`, `main_setup_connection()` PS2 local startup | Production initial/local-session map setup | preflight → unload → dispose → precache → `main_new_map()` | **Fix required when an old scenario/map is present** (e.g. an already loaded UI or reused local-session state). Even if cold boot normally has no loaded map, retain one safe order and document the conditional lifecycle contract rather than relying on an empty-map assumption. |

| `source/main/main.c:1524-1552`, `hcu_step8_test_start_local_map()` | Test-only entry used to start the Step 8 local workload | preflight → unload → dispose → precache | **Fix required for fixture fidelity.** This is the route that transitions the startup UI into the workload map; currently it contradicts `step8_workload_cleanup()` and can itself reproduce the order bug. Mark the test-only code with `port:`/diagnostic scope and test the real sequence after correction. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:64-72`, capacity-diagnostic initial UI release | Test-only | menu unload → game unload → dispose | **Fix required for diagnostic fidelity** when UI scenario is loaded. `main_menu_unload()` only clears shell/music flags ([`main.c:1130-1137`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1130)); it does not retire the scenario/tag owner. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:336-348`, post-preflight-fault setup | Test-only M2 UI lifecycle diagnostic | menu unload → game unload → dispose → retry UI | **Fix required for diagnostic fidelity.** It disposes the old UI only after its tag owner has been released; this undermines the lifecycle regression’s ownership premise even if its assertions happen to pass on a given build. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:289-296`, Step 8 workload cleanup | Test-only | dispose → unload | **Correct ordering; retain.** This is the source-backed invariant the other test-only teardown paths should match. |

| `source/main/main.c:2944-2955`, `main_reset_map_private()` | Production in-map BSP reset, not full map unload | switch BSP → dispose old-map transient state → reinitialize | **Do not blindly add `game_unload()`.** This does not release the full map owner; it is an in-place BSP/game reset. Keep it as a separate transition class and regression-check that no new full-owner release is introduced. |

| `source/main/main.c:2486-2487`, `main_exit()` | Process/game shutdown | dispose old-map → full game dispose; no `game_unload()` in this function | **Not the defective pair.** Verify outer shutdown has stopped map processing before global disposal, but do not treat this as a map replacement call site. |

| `source/networking/network_game_manager.c:801-805` | CE multiplayer map entry | dispose → unload | **Already correct in source.** Confirm the relevant PS2 local/network build actually includes this call path before adding any duplicate cleanup. |

The PS2 branches needing production source-marked ordering edits are therefore three `main.c` paths (map-name transition, return-to-UI, local startup) plus the test-only Step 8 start helper. Two diagnostic-only paths need order correction to avoid tests normalizing the bug. The network manager and in-map BSP reset are controls, not fixes.

Use one exact image and record ELF/source pins. In interpreter and recompiler, start from the loaded UI scenario, run UI→two-player Sidewinder workload, tick, dispose→unload back to a verified empty owner, then load UI and repeat a second map transition. Assert ordered markers for CE-dispose start/end while tag count and owner are live, CE unpublication, parent owner release, successful successor map load, gameplay workload completion, and clean teardown. Also test preflight refusal while the old UI/game map remains intact, followed by successful retry. No free-camera/render pixel claim is required for this teardown regression. The existing runner already checks workload success and empty-state markers ([`test_hcu_step8_mp_workload.py:27-58`](../../tools/test_hcu_step8_mp_workload.py#L27)); extend evidence to include order/identity, rather than accepting only the terminal marker.

verbatim_lines.raw: This audit expands the prior static BSP/scenario texture inventory to the gameplay content a multiplayer match can select. It is strictly the 13 named Halo CE multiplayer maps; campaign maps are not inputs. The audited maps are Beaver Creek, Blood Gulch, Boarding Action, Carousel, Chill Out, Damnation, Hang 'Em High, Longest, Prisoner, Putput, Rat Race, Sidewinder, and Wizard. Their current decompressed files' hashes match the earlier “retail map” inventory. The prior reports identify their extraction source as XISO SHA-256 `43ec0813edadd592b7b489a930f108d289db9313ac337611110ffca8be0a7258`, but that original XISO is not currently in `build/`; this pass verifies the extracted map bytes, not a fresh extraction from that XISO.

Across the 13 alternative maps, the unique path union contains 1,767 tag paths and the summed per-map tag-union count is 53,207,883 bytes. That sum is a catalog total, not a concurrent allocation. Blood Gulch is largest for the walked in-image tag union (4,260,147 bytes), MODL output (4,563,904), OTEX output (3,027,136), and combined static-TEXS/LM plus full-closure OTEX output (3,466,272). The latter is below the nominal 4,194,304-byte `texture_cache` reservation in [`config/memory-budget.json`](../../config/memory-budget.json#L13), but is not proof that those sections are actually owned by or resident in that arena.

The schema walk also records 894–897 `file_data` descriptors/map, with declared byte totals of 11,016,000–11,460,456 across the walked records. Reachable bitmap tags refer to 16,409,600–19,622,400 unique source pixel-interval bytes/map in the decompressed map inputs (Blood Gulch is 19,622,400). These are *input/source extents*, not a recommendation to retain raw bitmap pixels on EE RAM; the conversion pipeline moves selected render data to converted packs. The complete per-map breakdown and source flags are in the JSON. The raw in-image tag union alone is below the 6,815,744-byte `resident_gameplay` reservation, but is not the converted CTAG image size or a resident high-water result; relocation/compaction, stripped graphics fields, file-data ownership, CE global data, and allocator metadata still determine actual fit.

1. Scenario-selected object assets materially undercount a match's content. For Beaver Creek the prior selected object set was 12 models, 875,808-byte OTEX, and 371,248-byte ANIM; the closure contains 53 models, 2,759,776-byte OTEX, and 652,160-byte ANIM. Across maps, full closure OTEX is 2,273,344–3,027,136 bytes versus scenario-only OTEX 389,376–1,705,504 bytes in the companion inventory. The full closure adds 38–41 model tags and 14–17 animation-graph tags over the scenario/sky baseline, depending on the map.

3. Every audited retail MP map has 15 weapon tags, 14 equipment tags, 2 biped tags, 3 vehicle tags, and 16 projectile tags. The source-map name scan finds the Gravity Rifle in all 13 maps, but no Energy Sword or Fuel Rod tag in any of them. **The two requested custom weapons cannot be covered by this stock retail-MP closure:** their tag roots, models, FP models/animation, projectile/effect dependencies (Fuel Rod), converted assets, and runtime residency need a separately provisioned mod/port asset source and must be added to the acceptance closure. This is an asset-source gap, not an inference that those weapons cannot be implemented.

5. Dynamic gameplay pool constraints are a separate measurement. The pinned CE PS2 limits retain source/Xbox capacities, not accepted EE byte allocations: e.g. 2,048 object slots and a 1 MiB object pool are declared in [`halo_ps2_limits.h`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/include/halo_ps2_limits.h#L30), object initialization allocates the object data array and object memory pool ([`objects.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1039)), AI uses a 256-actor array ([`actors.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/actors.c#L564)), and particles allocate 1,024 × 0x70-byte data entries ([`particles.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/effects/particles.c#L230)). These allocations are routed via CE `game_state_data_new`/memory-pool ownership and cannot be equated with measured occupancy of the 2,621,440-byte `dynamic_simulation` reservation. A multiplayer acceptance fixture must measure actual allocations and high-water under maximum supported players/bots, vehicles, projectiles, effects, and simultaneous ordnance.

- [`world_load()`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L58) and [`world_load_objects()`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L103) load sections into a caller-supplied `arena_t`; these APIs alone do not prove the caller uses the `texture_cache` reservation for TEXS/LM/OTEX or that MODL/ANIM have a dedicated live owner. Step 8 must establish the actual caller/arena and measure retained bytes plus temporary source/decode overlap.

- The biggest measured pack-section subtotal here (TEXS + LM + full OTEX) is 3,466,272 bytes, but it does not establish cache fit: decoded source copies, GS upload staging, texture deduplication policy, fragmentation, simultaneous map transition, renderer pins, and arena routing are outside this offline conversion result. Likewise MODL at 4.35–4.61 MiB and ANIM at ~651 KiB are independent output sizes, not dynamic-pool occupancy.

1. Establish the production ownership path for every emitted section (including `MODL`, `OTEX`, `ANIM`, TEXS, and LM) from pack open to eviction/unload; instrument allocator owner, bytes, high-water, alignment, and retained source/decode staging on EE/PCSX2.

2. Add match fixtures that spawn the supported maximum local/network player and bot mix, switch through all weapons (including the custom Energy Sword and Fuel Rod provision), mount each vehicle, and exercise representative projectiles/effects. Record dynamic-pool and texture-owner peaks and fail on exhaustion; preserve replay/state parity.

3. Derive the special-weapon asset closure from their actual tag roots and conversion input, then rerun the same closure/conversion measurement. Do not mark the static asset subcheck or Step 8 capacity gate complete based on retail maps alone.

This work closes a previously missing, reproducible *offline content inventory* slice of Step 8. It does not close Step 7's target-sized BSP-query dependency, the runtime owner/high-water tests, the special-weapon asset gap, or Step 8 as a whole.

verbatim_lines.raw: # M2 Step 8: static render-asset inventory for 13 stock multiplayer maps

I generated a reproducible, per-map inventory of converted BSP textures (`TEXS`), all converted lightmap sections (`LMn`), and scenario-selected object textures (`OTEX`) for the complete 13-map stock multiplayer set. This addresses the *offline static converted-section size* subquestion in Step 8; it is not a runtime cache high-water measurement, map-admission proof, or all-render-state bound.

The largest converted static texture-section sum is Blood Gulch at **2,144,640 bytes** (2.045 MiB); Sidewinder is next at 1,838,656 bytes. All 13 maps together sum to 14,880,288 bytes, but that is an *across-alternatives catalog total* and must not be charged as simultaneous live memory. Each row is the sum of one map's `TEXS` + scenario-selected `OTEX` + all its converted `LMn` sections. These rows do not include BSP geometry, object MODL/SCEN/ANIM/SKY sections, runtime-created effects, weapons, UI, DMA staging, decoded Xbox source buffers, cache fragmentation, or transition overlap.

The measured largest row is below the configured 4,194,304-byte `texture_cache` reservation in [`config/memory-budget.json`](../../config/memory-budget.json#L13), but this is not proof that those bytes are allocated from that reservation today. The parent/halo-ps2 section loader takes a caller-supplied arena and copies section payloads there; `world_load()` retains BSP, TEXS, and the selected LM section in its `arena` argument, and `world_load_objects()` retains MODL/SCEN and optional OTEX in its supplied arena ([`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L58), [`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L103), [`section.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/section.c#L153)). Therefore the sums are asset sizes that an ownership design must place, not evidence that the current 4 MiB reservation is the allocator backing them or that concurrent live working set fits. The renderer consumes TEXS/LM payloads as source views ([`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L5), [`tex.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/tex.c#L24)); these data are not evidence of a measured residency/eviction policy.

The isolated audit is [`tools/audit_mp_render_asset_bound.py`](../../tools/audit_mp_render_asset_bound.py#L1). verbatim_lines.raw: The current sources do not expose a per-map dynamic simulation high-water, so no honest byte estimate for bots, co-op, projectiles, effects, and moving objects can be derived from the 13 scenario files alone. The actionable source-backed bound is the allocator and fixed-pool ownership:

| PS2 dynamic simulation | 2,621,440 B (`dynamic_pool`) | `hcu_memory_bind_parent_v2()` binds the entire region to CE's compatibility `malloc` arena. Allocation is 16-byte aligned and monotonic; frees inside that arena are no-ops. |

| CE object payload pool | 1,048,576 B | `objects_initialize()` allocates it via `game_state_memory_pool_new()`, hence inside `HALO_PORT_GAME_STATE_SIZE` in `resident_gameplay`. Do not add it to dynamic simulation while this route remains. |

| Actor / prop / swarm arrays | actors 256, props 768, swarms 32, components 256 | Each is created by `game_state_data_new()` and belongs to game state, not the dynamic malloc arena. These are datum-count caps, not byte high-water. |
| PS2 object slots | 2,048 per map | Header/data-array capacity; not a byte count and not evidence all slots are simultaneously active. |
| PS2 effect family caps | 256 effects, 1,024 particles, 64 particle systems, 256 contrails | Fixed count limits only; storage ownership and live bytes are not surfaced as a combined pool ledger. |

The isolated 1 MiB object memory pool is 40% of the 2.5 MiB dynamic arena by byte capacity, but that is only a hypothetical subtraction if the pool is rehomed. Under the present CE call route it is already charged to the game-state block in `resident_gameplay`; charging it again would double count. The rest of the 2.5 MiB arena has no published consumer ledger or high-water, and no source or test currently proves that the remaining 2,621,440 B accommodates simultaneous match allocations.

This is scoped to exactly the 13 stock multiplayer maps and their multiplayer bot/co-op workload. Campaign content is excluded. The Step 8 map package/query fixture covers map ownership and selected BSP consumers; it explicitly does not instantiate the dynamic live-match owners, so its map-cycle high-water must not be reused as a simulation measurement.

- The memory map says the CE object pool is nested in the game-state provider and must not be charged twice; it records dynamic high-water as unknown: [`config/hcu-ps2-memory-map.json`](../../config/hcu-ps2-memory-map.json#L1-L8) and [line 80](../../config/hcu-ps2-memory-map.json#L80).

- The PS2 compatibility allocator aligns each request to 16 bytes, advances `malloc_used`, rejects overflow, and does not reclaim arena pointers on free: [`ps2_memory.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/src/ps2_memory.c#L288-L331).

- CE declares `OBJECT_MEMORY_POOL_SIZE` from the port constant and sets garbage thresholds as 5%, 10%, and 20% of that size: [`objects.h`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.h#L25-L37).

- Runtime initialization calls `game_state_memory_pool_new("objects", OBJECT_MEMORY_POOL_SIZE)` outside editor mode: [`objects.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1040-L1063). That helper obtains the pool bytes with `game_state_malloc()`: [`game_state.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L549-L566) and [pool constructor](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/saved%20games/game_state.c#L943-L955).

Instrument the real CE allocation boundaries in the combined no-bootstrap PS2 image with per-owner current/peak bytes and allocation-failure counts. Keep object-pool bytes separate from the dynamic allocator unless its allocation route is deliberately changed. Use one source-pinned MP map per row, then exercise a shared workload on all 13: four local players, configured maximum bots, co-op encounter spawn/cleanup, vehicle enter/exit, repeated projectile and grenade/effect lifecycles, and map unload/reload. Record source map SHA, ELF SHA, memory-budget hash, player/bot count, owner peaks, and whether frees/reloads restore allocator headroom. Run on PCSX2 interpreter and recompiler first, then target-sized EE if available.

The fixture must fail if an allocation returns null, if a count pool fills, if the dynamic arena cursor exceeds 2,621,440 B, or if reset/transition leaves the cursor elevated. A passing diagnostic would establish only that exact workload's peak; it would not prove arbitrary custom-game settings or Step 8 closure.

This report is a source-backed arithmetic/ownership audit. No executable per-map high-water artifact exists: the current PS2 allocator exposes no peak counter, and the retained 13-map candidate run omits live dynamic simulation. Scenario placement counts would not substitute for heap bytes or simultaneous lifetime evidence. Step 8 remains open until the live fixture supplies those measurements alongside the other map/render/audio owners.

owner is the high-water of co-resident converted section data in the candidate render owner. cache high-water is occupied texture pages under the actual renderer cache API; the 270-page limit reflects the current 512x448 NTSC mode and renderer's reserved pages, as derived below. uploads / hits / deferred list frame 0 then frame 1.

The runtime emits one row per map with scratch high-water 98,304 / 524,288 bytes. Selected MODL coverage ranged from 4 models / 23 parts on Putput to 25 models / 163 parts on Blood Gulch; these are converter model-section counts, not spawned-object counts.

- The production world.c:21-37 callback supplies mip 0, its pixel bytes, and the CLUT; world.c:43-57 supplies lightmap page pixels and the shared 1,024-byte CLUT. This fixture uses those same parser views.

- submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/render/bsp_render.c:29-33 reserves 16 texture-window pages for CLUTs and one for the font. Its pages_for and resident_tex0 at :344-382 compute page occupancy, charge pixel-plus-CLUT upload bytes, request a cache entry, and enqueue the real GS upload pair. :800-802 and :832-840 establish texture/lightmap/object key ordering and the 1.5 MiB budget.

- The page count used by the diagnostic follows platform/video.h (512x448, 4 MiB GS VRAM) and platform/video.c:14-29: the two CT16 framebuffers and Z24 buffer consume 1,835,008 bytes (224 GS pages), and bsp_render.c:164 starts the texture window after the extra allocated page. 512 total GS pages - 224 framebuffer/Z pages - 1 window-base page - 17 CLUT/font pages = 270 cache pages.

- Halo-64's `submodules/halo-64/port/n64/NOTES.md:115-155` is a useful comparison for why its texture policy cannot be copied: its first-person atlas had to be split into windows and represented as small CI4 textures, while it also describes tradeoffs around its level texture path. This measurement instead uses this repository's halo-ps2 GS/VRAM/cache implementation and its 270-page renderer window; no N64 texture or pool limit is imported.

In the default guarded layout, texture begins 16 bytes beyond the current BSP region, so the three candidate spans are not one contiguous candidate owner.

There is already an opt-in candidate recarve in `src/stream/hcu_main.c:192-228`, called only when `HALO_PS2_STEP8_MP_CAPACITY_DIAGNOSTIC` is defined at `src/stream/hcu_main.c:327-333`. It repartitions the same 10 MiB BSP+texture total into a 6,470,832-byte map region and 4,014,928-byte texture region, moving the boundary canary to the combined end. This pad-8 profile allocates 8 bytes more to BSP than the tail-inclusive natural minimum (1,993,704) and 8 bytes less to texture (4,014,936). The real parent binder then exposes the exact pad-8 candidate tag/BSP/texture capacities as adjacent views. No additional production carve change is warranted by this test alone: the candidate is diagnostic-only, map admission remains closed, and target texture residency/render behavior remains unqualified.

This is adjacent fixed spans, not one shared runtime allocation cursor. The CE port intentionally consumes separate tag, BSP, and texture-provider interfaces. The useful ownership invariant is therefore: one backing interval is partitioned into nonoverlapping adjacent views, while CE's tag and BSP stores retain their own semantic bounds. `src/stream/hcu_map_service.c:529-553` uses the streaming map-owner for HMAP/CRNG/CBIX preflight and passes the tag-cache size to CTAG validation; it does not own or allocate the renderer's texture data. CE's `ps2_cache.c:322-340` obtains its BSP base/capacity from the BSP provider. The selected PS2 CE sound/cache adapter is `port/ps2/src/ps2_sound_cache.c`, not the excluded Xbox LRU texture cache.

The `texture_cache` region at issue is used by the retained halo-ps2 GS texture-pack/cache path, while the candidate all-map host fixture loads converted `TEXS`, `LMn`, and selected `OTEX` resources into an adjacent owner and verifies capacity/high-water. That host fixture is useful coexistence evidence but does not establish that the actual EE recarve survives GS uploads, texture eviction/pins, animation/object asset overlap, or frame DMA. Continue using the measured PS2 owner and renderer tests; do not use the excluded Xbox LRU values as sizing authority.
production-binder-recarved tag=4477120 bsp=1993712 map=6470832 texture=4014928 total=10485760 unified_adjacent=1 parent_bytes_unchanged=1 guards=1 ready=1

`ready=1` in the first row demonstrates why startup readiness cannot replace per-profile capacity assertions. The second row proves only the binder-level recarve arithmetic and canary placement, not that all 13 maps pass loading, all renderer assets remain resident, or textures reach the GS.

2. Before promoting the candidate profile, connect this owner to the real halo-ps2 render-cache path and measure cache pages, pinning, eviction/reload, upload ordering, mip/lightmap/CLUT behavior, and guard integrity. Do not port or size from the excluded Xbox texture LRU; Halo-64 is only an architectural comparator, not PS2 capacity evidence.

3. Then use the recarved layout through the real map preflight, CTAG mount, BSP query/render-resource selection, renderer cache staging, and failure/reload flows on the required multiplayer map corpus. Require high-water and guard results at target/PCSX2; the current binder test is not that evidence.

4. Only after those results should the capacity profile/API be promoted out of the diagnostic path. Any later change should continue to partition the existing 10 MiB; no reserve or other region is authorized by this result.

`tests/test_hcu_mp_capacity.py` now reads each decompressed stock map's sole BSP, checks the source-layout extents, and independently extracts weather-palette entries, referenced wind-tag definitions, direction/magnitude fields, and every cluster's weather-palette selector (lines 69–127). Inputs are hash-pinned by map and package, and package conversion is tied to the audited schema ELF SHA-256 `2fba411b7244b20fdf31f0b1e540fc2b6f5598891f53a64f8b12f850a0cda0aa` (`tests/test_hcu_mp_capacity.py:15-48,202-225`). The generated source inventory is retained at `build/m2-mp-weather-wind-13/mp_weather_wind_source_inventory.json` (SHA-256 `549e10e47b5a59a0056f15924f094efbb7bf0d75c76a963bdb00548102dcbac5`); the source-derived C goldens contain 14 palette rows and 239 cluster rows (SHA-256 `fa333f74b40bcde3359ab51f169c49ef26056e1496e0a293d0c86d5a4fbf0404`).

The fixture loads each verified HP2 package through the existing map lifecycle. For the actual relocated CE BSP/tag data, `tests/hcu_mp_weather_wind_host32.c:76-140` verifies palette count, wind group/datum, direction and magnitude, plus every cluster selector against the separately read retail source. It fixes random seeds per map/reload, calls `random_math_initialize`, real CE `wind_initialize_for_new_map()` and `wind_update()`, then queries normal, simple, damped, and cluster-selected currents and checks NONE references return zero (`tests/hcu_mp_weather_wind_host32.c:142-206`). It disposes wind/random state before lifecycle unload/reload.

The production CE behavior under test is in `submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/scenario/wind.c:184-272` (state initialization/update and wind construction) and `:274-330` (palette query, damping, and invalid/NONE zero result). The source defines the embedded Euler fields as `{ yaw, pitch }` in `submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/math/real_math.h:396-401`.

The first elevated execution stopped on Longest because the independent vector oracle had interpreted the two variation-area floats in reverse order. The CE `wind_definition` embeds `real_euler_angles2d`, whose source layout is `{yaw, pitch}`; consequently the third float is yaw variation and the fourth is pitch variation. The source-derived oracle was corrected in `tests/test_hcu_wind_consumer.py:176-189` to model that declared order. This changed only expected-value construction, not CE implementation. The corrected current executable then passed the complete 26-row run above. This is specifically why the earlier failing log `build/m2-mp-weather-wind-13/native-run.log` (old executable; SHA-256 `c179999b389d458a780f4eb99b47e32e2db80028c635125bbc101795defaa0a9`) is not acceptance evidence.

The host harness intentionally uses diagnostic host-sized tag/BSP/claims storage, as documented in `tests/test_hcu_mp_capacity.py:228-230`. It therefore establishes source-backed CE wind behavior against relocated retail map data and repeated host lifecycle stability, not fit in PS2 EE memory, runtime performance, physical arena high-water, optical/OPL reads, sound playback, weather-particle drawing, or in-game visuals.
